title: The Degrees Of Divine Unity And The Passage To The 2nd Stopping Place

questions.question: What made the traveller speak to his own heart at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: He noticed that believers, especially people connected to a spiritual path, keep repeating words of Allah’s oneness, and this showed him that belief in Allah’s oneness has many levels.

questions.question: Which group is specially mentioned along with the people of faith?
questions.answer: People connected to a sufi order.

questions.question: What do their repeated words show about affirming Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: It is not just one simple idea; it has many degrees and deeper levels.

questions.question: How is affirming Allah’s unity described in the passage as an act of religion?
questions.answer: It is described as a joyful, precious, lofty, holy duty, a natural function, and an act of worship.

questions.question: Why does the traveller want to open the door to another stopping-place?
questions.answer: He wants to reach a higher level in understanding and affirming Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What kind of knowledge is rejected as not being the true affirmation of Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: A made-up or merely imagined kind of knowledge is rejected.

questions.question: What makes true affirmation of Allah’s unity more valuable than imagination-based thinking?
questions.answer: It is based on proof and real knowledge.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is true affirmation of Allah’s unity inside a person?
questions.answer: It is a settled judgment, confirmation, acceptance, and inward agreement.

questions.question: How does a person with true affirmation view Allah’s nearness to creation?
questions.answer: Such a person can recognize the Sustainer as present with all things.

questions.question: How does such a person look at the things in the world?
questions.answer: He sees every created thing as a sign and pathway leading to its Creator.

questions.question: What mistake does this person avoid when looking at the world?
questions.answer: He does not treat created things as barriers that hide Allah.

questions.question: What problem would happen if someone could not see Allah through creation?
questions.answer: That person would think he must push aside the whole universe first in order to find his Sustainer.

questions.question: After speaking to himself, at what door does the traveller knock?
questions.answer: He knocks at the door of Allah’s majesty and greatness.

questions.question: Where does he enter after that?
questions.answer: He enters the stopping-place of Allah’s actions and workings, the realm of creating and bringing things into being.

questions.question: What did he see there across the whole universe?
questions.answer: He saw five broad truths ruling throughout the cosmos and clearly proving Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What repeated practice of believers catches the traveller’s attention?
questions.answer: Their constant remembrance of Allah’s oneness and their repeating words that deny any god besides Him.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveller draw from that practice?
questions.answer: He understands that affirming Allah’s unity has different stages and depths.

questions.question: Besides being true, what feelings and values are connected to affirming Allah’s unity in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as deeply pleasant, highly valuable, and spiritually elevated.

questions.question: What does the passage say this affirmation is in terms of worship and human nature?
questions.answer: It is both an act of worship and a natural function built into a person.

questions.question: Why does the traveller say they should move on to another place of learning?
questions.answer: Because he wants to gain a further degree of understanding.

questions.question: What does the passage contrast with real knowledge of Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: It contrasts real knowledge with something imaginary or based only on mental pictures.

questions.question: On what foundation should true affirmation of Allah’s unity rest?
questions.answer: It should rest on evidence and proof.

questions.question: What four inner responses are included in true affirmation of Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: Judgment, confirmation, assent, and acceptance.

questions.question: How does this true affirmation change the way a person sees Allah in relation to all things?
questions.answer: It lets the person find his Lord with everything around him.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the role of created things?
questions.answer: Created things are signs that guide a person to the Creator.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should not be seen as blocking Allah’s presence?
questions.answer: Nothing in creation should be seen as a barrier to Him.

questions.question: What image is used to describe the wrong approach to finding the Sustainer?
questions.answer: The wrong approach is like needing to rip away the covering of the universe before reaching Him.

questions.question: What does the traveller call the world before entering the next stopping-place?
questions.answer: He calls it a place of instruction.

questions.question: What area does he enter after knocking?
questions.answer: He enters the realm of Divine actions and the world where things are made and brought forth.

questions.question: What was the result of entering that realm?
questions.answer: He witnessed five all-encompassing truths giving open proof of Divine unity.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the traveller first say to his heart about believers?
questions.answer: He says their constant words about Allah’s oneness point to the fact that tawhid has many levels.

questions.question: Which believers are especially highlighted in that statement?
questions.answer: Those linked to a sufi path are especially highlighted.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the spiritual worth of declaring Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: It is one of the most delightful, precious, and noble sacred responsibilities.

questions.question: What shows that this declaration is not only formal worship but also part of human nature?
questions.answer: The passage says it is an instinctive function as well as worship.

questions.question: What goal pushes the traveller to continue his journey?
questions.answer: He wants to reach a higher stage of true understanding of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What false idea about knowing Allah’s unity is pushed aside?
questions.answer: The idea that it is just a vague, imagined kind of knowing is pushed aside.

questions.question: How is true affirmation different from mere imagination?
questions.answer: It stands against imagination and comes from proof-based knowledge.

questions.question: What kind of inward certainty is true affirmation said to be?
questions.answer: It is a firm inner approval and acceptance.

questions.question: What ability does this certainty give to the heart?
questions.answer: It enables the heart to recognize its Sustainer together with all things.

questions.question: How should a believer understand the world if he has this certainty?
questions.answer: He should understand every part of the world as opening a way to its Creator.

questions.question: What should a believer refuse to think about created things?
questions.answer: He should refuse to think they prevent Allah’s nearness or hide Him completely.

questions.question: What would someone have to do if he saw the cosmos as a barrier?
questions.answer: He would feel he had to remove that covering in order to reach his Sustainer.

questions.question: What does the traveller do after encouraging himself onward?
questions.answer: He goes to the door of Allah’s majesty and greatness.

questions.question: What new stopping-place does he enter?
questions.answer: He enters the station of Divine acts and the realm of creation and origination.

questions.question: What did he witness in that stopping-place?
questions.answer: He witnessed five great truths spread across the universe that clearly testify to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What behavior of the people of faith leads the traveller to think more deeply?
questions.answer: Their ongoing remembrance of Allah’s unity and repeated declaration of it.

questions.question: Why does that behavior suggest that Allah’s unity has many degrees?
questions.answer: Because people keep returning to it again and again, which shows it contains deep levels to be realized.

questions.question: How is affirming Allah’s unity described in terms of its sweetness and rank?
questions.answer: It is described as very enjoyable and very exalted.

questions.question: What two religious descriptions are given for affirming Allah’s unity besides its value?
questions.answer: It is called a sacred duty and an act of worship.

questions.question: What step does the traveller decide to take for greater understanding?
questions.answer: He decides to open the door to another stopping-place in the house of instruction.

questions.question: What kind of “knowledge” does the traveller say is not enough?
questions.answer: Mere imagined or unreal knowledge is not enough.

questions.question: What gives true affirmation of Allah’s unity its strength?
questions.answer: Its strength comes from proof and certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage say true affirmation includes besides knowing?
questions.answer: It includes confirming, agreeing, and accepting.

questions.question: How close is the Sustainer understood to be by the person with true affirmation?
questions.answer: The person can find the Sustainer present with everything.

questions.question: What does the person with true affirmation notice in every created thing?
questions.answer: He notices a way leading from it to its Maker.

questions.question: Why is it important not to treat creation as a wall or screen?
questions.answer: Because doing so would make a person think Allah can only be found after getting past the universe.

questions.question: What phrase shows the traveller is moving with determination?
questions.answer: He tells himself to go forward.

questions.question: Which Divine qualities are mentioned at the door he approaches?
questions.answer: Allah’s sublimity and grandeur.

questions.question: What kind of world does he enter after that?
questions.answer: The world of creation and bringing things into existence.

questions.question: What was spread over the whole cosmos in that world?
questions.answer: Five wide-reaching truths that openly prove Divine unity.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do believers often repeat and announce?
questions.answer: They often repeat and proclaim Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does this repeating teach the traveller about tawhid?
questions.answer: It teaches him that tawhid includes many stages of understanding.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the importance of affirming Allah’s unity in a believer’s life?
questions.answer: It presents it as a noble, precious, and joyful religious responsibility.

questions.question: What does the passage say about its connection to worship?
questions.answer: It is itself a holy act of worship.

questions.question: Why does the traveller seek another stopping-place?
questions.answer: He wants to gain a further level of true affirmation.

questions.question: What is lacking in an understanding based only on imagination?
questions.answer: It lacks proof and real certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage call the stronger kind of affirmation?
questions.answer: It calls it a real knowledge that comes from evidence and leads to firm acceptance.

questions.question: What inward actions belong to this true affirmation?
questions.answer: A person judges it to be true, confirms it, assents to it, and accepts it.

questions.question: What is one sign that a person has reached this level?
questions.answer: He can sense his Sustainer’s presence along with all things.

questions.question: How does this person use the things around him?
questions.answer: He uses them as signs that guide him to the Creator.

questions.question: What wrong view of the universe is rejected?
questions.answer: The view that the universe blocks a person from Allah is rejected.

questions.question: If someone held that wrong view, what would he think he needed to do?
questions.answer: He would think he had to strip away the universe like a covering before finding Allah.

questions.question: What does the traveller do when he reaches the next stage of the journey?
questions.answer: He knocks at the door of Allah’s majesty and greatness.

questions.question: Into what realm is he admitted?
questions.answer: Into the realm of Divine deeds and the world of creation and origination.

questions.question: What did he observe there that relates to Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: He observed five comprehensive truths dominating the cosmos and clearly proving Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What repeated religious practice is mentioned at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: Believers repeatedly remember and declare that only Allah is truly worthy of worship.

questions.question: Which believers are given special mention in this practice?
questions.answer: Those associated with a sufi order.

questions.question: What does this repeated practice reveal about belief in Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: It reveals that this belief has many degrees, not just one level.

questions.question: In what three ways is this affirmation praised before the traveller moves on?
questions.answer: It is praised as delightful, valuable, and lofty.

questions.question: What does the traveller hope to gain by opening another stopping-place?
questions.answer: He hopes to reach a higher degree of understanding and affirming Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What sort of understanding is not the true tawhid he is looking for?
questions.answer: Not a merely imagined or unreal kind of understanding.

questions.question: What sort of understanding is he looking for instead?
questions.answer: One based on proof, certainty, and real knowledge.

questions.question: What does the passage say true affirmation does in the heart and mind?
questions.answer: It settles into a person as firm approval, confirmation, and acceptance.

questions.question: How does this help a person relate to the world around him?
questions.answer: It helps him recognize Allah with all things and see signs of the Creator everywhere.

questions.question: What should every created thing become for such a person?
questions.answer: A road or pointer leading to its Maker.

questions.question: What should nothing in creation become for such a person?
questions.answer: An obstacle to Allah’s presence.

questions.question: What does the passage imply is difficult about a weaker faith?
questions.answer: A weaker faith may feel the need to get past the universe first before finding the Sustainer.

questions.question: After speaking to himself, what door does the traveller approach?
questions.answer: The door of Allah’s grandeur and majesty.

questions.question: What is the name of the place he enters next?
questions.answer: The stopping-place of Allah’s acts and workings, the realm of creation and origination.

questions.question: What did he discover filling that realm?
questions.answer: Five universal truths that clearly testify to Divine unity.
